t.r: Nijūmuragō, Ojiya and Yamakoshi, Niigata Prefecture, Japan
t.d: Farmers in the 'twenty villages' bred red and white carp with black ones to produce the first coloured koi.
t.tech: selective breeding

t.r: Indian subcontinent; Britain from the 19th century
t.d: Head massage with hair oil, the origin of the word shampoo, brought to Brighton by Dean Mahomed.
t.tech: Massaging oil into scalp and hair

t.d: Traditional extraction of argan oil, mostly by rural women, for food, medicine and cosmetics including hair care.
t.tech: Harvesting, drying, pulping, grinding, sorting and hand-milling kernels, then mixing with warm water
ctr: Women's cooperatives in the Arganeraie reserve
t.auth: Cooperative-made oil from the Moroccan reserve; very cheap 'pure argan' is suspect given the labour-intensive yield

t.d: Hot-air bathing at 80–110 °C with löyly from water on the stones of a kiuas, alternated with cooling off.
t.tech: wood or electric stove with stones; löyly; birch whisking
t.auth: wood stove with stone mass; sessions with vihta/vasta whisk

t.d: Deep, square soaking bath entered after washing, traditionally wooden (hinoki) or a wood-fired cast-iron goemon-buro.
t.tech: soak at 38–42 °C after rinsing; wood-fired kettle in goemon-buro
t.auth: deep square tub; no overflow; hinoki wood

t.d: Wood-heated steam bath with venik whisking, in black (smoke) or white (piped) form.
t.tech: stove with firebox, stone chamber and water tank; venik
t.auth: three-room plan; venik; felt hat

t.p: Umayyad period onwards; classical peak 16th century
t.d: Steam bath descended from Roman thermae, with warm and hot rooms and a heated marble navel stone.
t.tech: furnace and hypocaust; steam
t.auth: marble göbek taşı; domed hot room with skylights

t.d: Chimneyless smoke sauna tradition including bathing customs, whisk-making, sauna building and meat smoking.
t.tech: stone-covered stove without chimney; smoke vented before bathing
t.auth: no chimney; raised platform; smoke-blackened interior

t.d: Yoruba-origin soap made from the ash of plant peels and bark mixed with plant oils.
t.tech: sun-dried plant matter burned to ash for alkali, then cooked with water and oils
t.mat: plantain skins, palm leaves, cocoa pods, shea bark, palm kernel and other plant oils
t.auth: dark, uneven colour from plant ash

t.r: Aleppo, Syria (also made in Turkey and Damascus by relocated makers)
t.d: Hand-made hot-process olive-oil soap with laurel-berry oil, cut, stamped and aged for months.
t.tech: three-day boil in in-ground vats, laurel oil added last, poured on the floor, trodden smooth, cut, hand-stamped and cured in stacked towers
t.mat: olive oil, laurel-berry oil, lye, water
t.auth: laurel and olive scent, no animal fat or colour; laurel oil above 16% rated higher; widely imitated

t.d: Red dye painted on hands and feet at weddings and festivals.
t.tech: applied with cotton swab or brush
t.mat: red lac; now mainly synthetic dye
t.auth: Natural alta is lac-based; most current alta is synthetic.

t.r: India, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and diaspora
t.d: Forehead dot worn by Hindus, Jains and Buddhists, red or maroon after sindoor and kumkum, now often a sticker.
t.tech: painted with powder, or self-adhesive felt or metal
t.mat: kumkum, sindoor, lac, felt, thin metal
t.auth: Traditional bindi is painted; lac tikli preceded modern stickers.

t.p: Formalised in the Ming dynasty (1368–1644); facial use popular worldwide from 2016–2022
t.d: Traditional Chinese practice of scraping oiled skin with a smooth tool, with a lighter facial form and the related jade roller.
t.tech: Firm one-way strokes over lubricated skin; lighter pressure for the face
t.mat: Jade and other stones, ceramic spoons, coins, water buffalo horn
ctr: Palace Museum, Beijing (Qing jade roller set)
t.auth: Antique pieces are museum-held; modern tools are mass-made, so judge by stone and finish rather than claims of tradition.

t.r: Middle East, North Africa, Turkey, Balkans, Central Asia
t.d: Islamic steam-bath tradition inherited from Roman thermae, with soaping, scrubbing and massage by attendants.
t.tech: steam heat, soaping, scrubbing with a rough mitt, massage
t.mat: black soap (Morocco), olive-oil soaps, kese mitt, peştemal cloth
t.auth: kese is a rough scrubbing mitten; peştemal a silk or cotton body cloth

t.n: Henna: rituals, aesthetic and social practices
t.r: Arab states and North Africa (UAE, Algeria, Bahrain, Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Mauritania, Morocco, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Sudan, Tunisia, Yemen)
t.p: ancient to present; UNESCO Representative List 2024
t.d: Henna body art and rites such as the Night of the Henna, inscribed by UNESCO on a 16-state nomination.
t.tech: leaf powder mixed to a paste, applied by stick or syringe, left to stain
t.auth: Real henna stains reddish-brown and darkens over a day or two; 'black henna' that stains black fast contains PPD and can cause severe allergy and scarring.

t.p: Modern; spread from Japan to Asia, the US, then Europe
t.d: Japanese skincare culture of gentle layered steps and local ingredients, carried abroad by Shiseido, Kanebo, Shu Uemura, DHC and SK-II.
t.tech: Double cleansing, layering from lightest to heaviest texture, kobido facial massage
t.mat: Yuzu, camellia oil, rice, green tea, konjac
t.auth: Check brand origin and country of manufacture on the label.

t.p: Known in the West from 2011 (BB cream) onward
t.d: Korean skincare culture of long layered routines aimed at hydrated, luminous 'glass skin'.
t.tech: Multi-step layering: oil and water cleansing, essences, serums, sheet masks, moisturiser, sunscreen
t.mat: Green tea, orchid, soybean, snail mucin, bee venom
t.auth: Check brand origin and country of manufacture on the label.

t.d: Soot-based kajal and mineral surma worn by women and children, also against the evil eye and in classical dance.
t.tech: kajal: soot from burning oil or ghee mixed with oil; surma: ground mineral
t.mat: soot, ghee, camphor, sandalwood; galena or other minerals
t.auth: Both have been linked to chemical toxicity, especially lead; prefer products with ingredient lists.

t.r: Egypt, Middle East, North and West Africa
t.d: Mineral eye cosmetic worn by Egyptians of all classes and spread through Arabia, North Africa and West Africa.
t.tech: crushing mineral to fine powder; applied with a stick
t.mat: stibnite (antimony sulfide); modern often galena (lead sulfide), charcoal
ctr: Hausa, Fulani, Tuareg and Yoruba peoples
t.auth: Many traditional kohls contain lead; the FDA warns against kohl, kajal, al-kahal, surma, tiro, tozali and kwalli for lead poisoning risk.

t.d: South Asian henna art on hands, wrists, forearms and feet for weddings, religious festivals and family ceremonies.
t.tech: paste piped from a plastic cone, brush or stick; dries, cracks and is left to stain
t.mat: henna powder, water or lemon, oils
t.auth: Body-art-quality henna is finely sifted; avoid PPD 'black henna' (Florida Department of Health, FDA warnings).

t.p: significant industry by the 14th century; UNESCO ICH (urgent safeguarding) 2024
t.d: Olive-oil soap tradition of Nablus, cut into cubes, stamped with a family or factory seal and dried in tall cones.
t.tech: cooking by Al Tabbeekha, spreading and setting, cutting by Al Bikar, hand-stamping by Al Khatimeh, drying in hollow stacked cones
t.mat: virgin olive oil, water, sodium hydroxide
t.auth: ivory colour, almost no scent, factory seal stamped on each cube

t.p: c. 1370 to present; name regulated by the Edict of Colbert 1688
t.d: Cauldron-made vegetable-oil soap sold in stamped blocks and cubes, used for body and laundry.
t.tech: Marseille process in cauldrons: mashing, salting-out, boiling and further steps over days
t.mat: olive oil or palm and coconut oils, lye, sea salt
t.auth: UPSM collective mark; hard homogenous soap in traditional geometric shapes, cauldron-made; no whimsical shapes

t.d: Red powders marking marital status in the hair parting (sindoor) and worn as forehead marks (kumkum).
t.tech: turmeric dried and powdered with slaked lime, alum or lime turns it red
t.mat: turmeric, alum, slaked lime; historically vermilion or red lead
t.auth: Herbal turmeric-based powder is non-toxic; some commercial sindoor contains lead (FDA warning on Swad sindoor).

t.d: China's main centre of firework and firecracker making for over 1,400 years, exporting since 1875.
t.tech: hand and factory filling of paper-cased crackers and shells
t.auth: Liuyang fireworks are a protected origin product

t.d: Japanese art of flower arrangement (kadō, 'way of the flower') rooted in Buddhist flower offerings.
t.tech: asymmetric arrangement of seasonal flowers, branches, stones and moss; stems held on a kenzan, cut with hanabasami
t.mat: seasonal flowers and branches; ceramic, glass, wood, bamboo or metal containers
t.auth: school certificates and teaching ranks; arrangements follow a school's named styles

t.d: Hard Lebkuchen from Aachen with protected origin.
t.tech: baked spiced dough
t.auth: maker located in or near Aachen (PGI)

t.d: Brewing of malted-maize beer, taught to women in the Inca aqlla wasi and used in feasts, alliances and rites.
t.tech: Germinated maize milled, boiled and fermented for days, then sieved through cloth
t.auth: Brewed from jora maize and served from clay chomba, wooden qero or gourd poto.

t.d: Community-conserved native potato landraces, kept in Peru's Potato Park near Cusco with the International Potato Center.
t.tech: community seed conservation
ctr: Potato Park (Parque de la Papa), Sacred Valley
t.auth: grown by the six Quechua communities of the Potato Park

t.d: Traditional distilled rice soju of Andong, tied to the Yuan-era supply base and recorded in the 17th-century Ŭmsik timibang.
t.tech: Brewing a grain mash and distilling it in a soju gori still

t.d: Caviar from sturgeon raised, farmed and slaughtered in France after wild Gironde fishing was banned.
t.tech: Siberian sturgeon farmed up to nine years, roe graded grain by grain and lightly salted
t.auth: Caviar d'Aquitaine collective trademark (2013), IGP in preparation

t.d: Lightly roasted coffee boiled unfiltered with cardamom and served unsweetened in small cups; on UNESCO's intangible heritage list.
t.tech: roasting in a mihmas, pounding in a mihbaj, boiling without filtering
t.mat: Arabica, cardamom, sometimes cloves or saffron
t.auth: Dallah pot, finjan cups, three cups poured partway

t.d: French artisan know-how and culture of baguette bread, on the UNESCO intangible heritage lists since 2022.
t.tech: Hand-shaped long loaves; tradition dough of flour, water, yeast and salt only (Décret Pain 1993)
t.auth: Sold as "baguette de tradition" only if made without additives or pre-made dough

t.d: Farmhouse raw cow's-milk cheese of Portuguese origin, registered by IPHAN as Brazilian intangible heritage in 2008.
t.tech: raw milk, rennet and 'pingo' whey starter, hand pressing, open-air maturing
t.auth: Raw milk; regional geographical indication or registered producer

t.d: The making, pouring and shared drinking of natural cider in Asturias, inscribed by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage in 2024.
t.tech: Natural fermentation of Asturian apples in cider mills; pouring from a height to aerate
t.auth: 100% Asturian apples; DOP Sidra de Asturias label

t.r: Belgium, Netherlands, Italy, England (formerly Austria, United States)
t.p: Monastic brewing since 1836 (Westmalle); ITA label from 1997
t.d: Label of the International Trappist Association for beers and goods made at Trappist abbeys under monastic supervision.
t.tech: Brewed within the immediate surroundings of the abbey under the supervision of monks or nuns; profits go to the community and charity
t.mat: Barley malt, hops, sugar, abbey yeast strains
t.auth: Hexagonal 'Authentic Trappist Product' logo on the label; 'abbey beer' or licensed brands such as Leffe or St. Bernardus are not Trappist.

t.d: Okinawan rice spirit distilled with indigenous black koji and aged as kusu in clay pots; UNESCO-listed in 2024 among Japan's traditional koji knowledge.
t.tech: Single fermentation of steamed long-grain rice fully converted with black koji, single pot distillation, long ageing in clay pots
t.mat: Thai indica or Okinawan rice, black koji (Aspergillus luchuensis), clay pots
t.auth: 'Ryukyu Awamori' GI label (since 2004); age claim for kusu means at least the stated years

t.r: Portugal, with fish from Norway and Iceland
t.d: Dry-salted cod, a Portuguese staple adopted from Basque salting off Newfoundland.
t.tech: cod gutted, salted and air-dried
t.auth: TSG label Bacalhau de Cura Tradicional Portuguesa

t.p: more than a century (style after Märzen)
t.d: Bamberg brewers' tradition of lager brewed from malt kilned over open beechwood fires.
t.tech: Malt dried over beechwood log fires; beer lagered in cool cellars
t.auth: Brewed in Bamberg with in-house fire-kilned malt rather than industrial smoked malt; Slow Food Ark of Taste listing (2017).

t.d: Sagardotegi cider houses where still cider is drawn straight from the barrel at the call of txotx during the season from 19 January.
t.tech: Double fermentation and maturing in oak or chestnut barrels

t.d: Caramelised or spiced biscuits of the Low Countries, listed in Brussels' intangible heritage inventory in 2020.
t.tech: moulded or cut biscuit

t.d: Crisp spiced noodle snack made as a cottage industry around Bikaner.
t.tech: dough of moth-bean and gram flour with spices pressed into fine strands and deep-fried
t.mat: Vigna aconitifolia (moth bean), gram flour, spices
t.auth: light yellow, crunchier and more strongly flavoured than sev; made in Bikaner

t.d: Twice-baked almond biscuits of Prato following Antonio Mattei's recipe.
t.tech: baked as a log, sliced and baked again

t.p: recorded in the 11th century; golden age under the Ottomans
t.d: Thick fermented grain drink sold by boza makers and street vendors in winter.
t.tech: ground cereal fermented and kept cool
t.auth: thick, tart, about 1% alcohol; served cold in winter

t.r: United Kingdom and Ireland (also Denmark, Australia)
t.d: Lettered peppermint sticks of boiled sugar made and sold at seaside resorts.
t.tech: letters built from strips of coloured sugar, assembled in spelling order, then the block stretched thin
t.mat: boiled sugar, peppermint or spearmint flavouring, colourings
t.auth: lettering runs through the whole stick; made on site at the resort

t.r: Cantal and Aubrac, Massif Central, France
t.p: Ancient; Salers produced for at least 2,000 years
t.d: Summer cheesemaking in stone mountain huts (burons) from pasture milk, producing large pressed tommes such as Salers and Laguiole.
t.tech: Raw milk renneted in a wooden gerle, curd pressed uncooked in large moulds, cave-matured
t.mat: Raw Salers, Aubrac or Simmental cows' milk
t.auth: PDO name on the rind; Salers only farmhouse-made between 15 April and 15 November; Laguiole bears a bull stamp and aluminium plaque.

t.d: Melon-and-almond calissons made mostly in Aix.
t.tech: candied melon and orange ground with almonds, iced and cut to an almond shape
t.mat: candied melon, orange, almonds, royal icing
t.auth: name protected in France since 1991

t.r: Cantabria and the Basque Country, Spain
t.d: Hand-processed canning of bonito del norte and anchovies on the Bay of Biscay coast, in oil or escabeche.
t.tech: loins cooked in salt water, cleaned by hand, packed in olive oil or escabeche and sterilised in an autoclave
t.auth: check the can names Thunnus alalunga, not atún claro

t.d: Wind-dried and cured pork and duck eaten with rice, especially in autumn and winter.
t.tech: Marinating in soy, Shaoxing wine and spices, then hanging to dry.
t.mat: Pork belly, pork and fat, duck.

t.r: Caspian and Black Sea, Iran and Russia
t.d: Salt-cured roe of wild beluga, ossetra and sevruga sturgeon, the traditional meaning of caviar, now replaced largely by farmed roe.
t.tech: ovaries removed, sieved, rinsed, salted malossol-style, graded and tinned
t.mat: beluga, ossetra and sevruga roe, salt
t.auth: CITES-labelled tins with species named

t.p: Ancient; kefir found in Bronze Age graves c. 3,600 years old
t.d: Grain-fermented milk of North Caucasian, notably Circassian, tradition that spread through the Soviet Union and worldwide.
t.tech: 2–5% kefir grains in milk for 12–24 hours at 20–25 °C, then strained and reused
t.mat: cow's, goat's or sheep's milk, traditionally raw
t.auth: Made with living kefir grains (bacteria and yeasts in a kefiran matrix), not only a powdered starter

t.r: Mongolia, Central Asia and the Caucasus
t.p: Nomadic pastoral tradition; dried yoghurt recorded in Arabic cookbooks from the 10th century
t.d: Pastoral dairy foods (tsagaan idee) eaten fresh in summer and dried into curd and yoghurt balls for winter.
t.tech: Churning yoghurt to remove butter, boiling and draining buttermilk curd, shaping and sun-drying for weeks
t.mat: Cow, yak, sheep, goat or mare's milk; salt
t.auth: Sun-dried, hand-shaped pieces with texture varying by animal; traditional qurut made from churned buttermilk rather than oven-fermented yoghurt.

t.p: Described by Herodotus (5th century BC) and William of Rubruck (13th century)
t.d: Fermented mare's milk of Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Bashkir, Kalmyk, Mongol and Yakut peoples.
t.tech: Liquid starter of lactobacilli and yeasts; mildly alcoholic (0.7–2.5%)
t.auth: Made from mare's milk; industrial versions use cow's milk adjusted with sucrose or whey

t.p: Han dynasty onward; popular from the Song dynasty (960–1279)
t.d: Making bean curd by coagulating soy milk and pressing the curds, credited by legend to Prince Liu An.
t.tech: grinding soaked soybeans, boiling, coagulating with gypsum or bittern, pressing; fermenting and drying

t.d: Sicilian cold-worked chocolate brought under Spanish rule, kept grainy because the sugar never dissolves.
t.tech: worked "a freddo" below 40 °C, not conched; once rolled on lava stone, poured into pewter moulds as thick bars
t.mat: cocoa with its butter, sugar; optional cinnamon, vanilla, ginger, chilli, almonds, citrus peel
ctr: Consorzio di Tutela del Cioccolato di Modica (2003)
t.auth: PGI mark; grainy rough texture, small air bubbles, crumbly break, slightly grey bloom; no milk, vegetable fat or lecithin

t.p: Named in the 12th century; earlier roots
t.d: Sun-dried-grape dessert wine from 14 villages in the Troödos foothills, protected by Cypriot law of 1990 and EU PDO.
t.tech: Sun-drying grapes 7–10 days before pressing
t.auth: Commandaria PDO

t.d: Sugared almonds of Sulmona, used as favours and arrangements.
t.tech: almonds panned in layers of sugar
t.auth: listed as a prodotto agroalimentare tradizionale (PAT)

t.d: Hand rolling of premium cigars by torcedores from tobacco grown in the Vuelta Abajo.
t.tech: Hand rolling (totalmente a mano) by torcedores, mostly women today
t.mat: Tobacco from Vuelta Abajo and Semi Vuelta, Pinar del Río
t.auth: Boxes and labels carry 'Hecho en Cuba'; 'Totalmente a mano' marks fully handmade cigars.

t.r: Darjeeling and Kalimpong, West Bengal, India
t.d: Himalayan black tea famed for muscatel flavour, sold by flush.
t.tech: long withering, rolling, oxidation on trays, firing
t.auth: India's first GI (2004); EU PGI 2011; Tea Board logo certification mark

t.d: Christmas fruit stollen baked by Dresden bakers.
t.tech: yeast dough with macerated fruit, sugared
t.mat: butter, dried and candied fruit, almonds
t.auth: seal showing Augustus the Strong

t.d: Handmade raw-milk cheese made on Dutch farms from at least half the farm's own milk.
t.tech: Raw-milk pressed-curd cheesemaking on the farm, often with cumin or other seeds and herbs
t.mat: Raw cow's, goat's, sheep's or buffalo milk
t.auth: Boerenkaas TSG name; raw milk, at least half from the producing farm

t.d: Copper top-fermented ale brewed and poured in Düsseldorf's old-town house breweries.
t.tech: top fermentation, cold conditioning
t.auth: House alt drawn on the premises in the Altstadt; Sticke released on set days.

t.r: Rwanda, Burundi, Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, DR Congo
t.d: Fermenting juice of East African Highland bananas with roasted sorghum or millet for rituals and ceremonies.
t.tech: Ripe bananas juiced and diluted, mixed with ground roasted sorghum and fermented
t.mat: Highland bananas (igikashi, igisahira), sorghum, millet or maize flour
t.auth: Made from Highland cooking-type bananas with grain, low alcohol, unbottled.

t.d: Water-pipe smoking of sweetened muʽassel tobacco, called shisha in Egypt and arjīlah in the Levant.
t.tech: Molasses-fermented tobacco smoked over charcoal
t.auth: Sealed packs from named makers such as Al Fakher and Nakhla.

t.d: Grafted orchards of named local dessert and culinary apples, kept alive in estates, walled gardens and community orchards.
t.tech: grafting onto rootstocks; standard and espalier training
t.mat: apple, pear, plum, cherry, damson trees
ctr: English Heritage orchards at Walmer Castle, Mount Grace Priory, Barnard Castle, Osborne
t.auth: Named cultivars propagated by grafting, not seed

t.d: Household ritual of roasting, grinding and brewing coffee in a clay jebena for three rounds.
t.tech: pan roasting, mukecha grinding, jebena boiling, three rounds (abol, tona, baraka)
t.mat: Green coffee, clay jebena, handleless cups, incense
t.auth: Jebena pot, three rounds, hosted by the woman of the household

t.d: Honey wine flavoured with gesho, made at home and sold in tej houses.
t.tech: Honey water fermented with boiled gesho stems and leaves, stirred daily, filtered
t.auth: Cloudy yellow, sweet, slightly effervescent; served in a berele

t.p: Farmhouse tradition to present; EU TSG
t.d: Farmhouse brewing of unboiled barley and rye ale lautered through juniper in a kuurna.
t.tech: Long step mash, lautering through juniper twigs, no boil, top fermentation with baking yeast
t.auth: Cloudy, barely carbonated, banana and juniper notes; TSG rules on process and ingredients.

t.d: Branch of French cuisine devoted to prepared meat products, mainly pork: ham, sausage, terrines, confit.
t.tech: Salt-curing and brining, forcemeats, fermentation.

t.d: Persian nougat traditionally made with psyllid manna from Zagros shrubs.
t.tech: egg white and manna or sugar beaten with nuts and rosewater
t.mat: psyllid manna, egg white, pistachios, almonds, rosewater
t.auth: traditional gaz uses manna rather than sugar and corn syrup

t.d: Pistachio baklava of Gaziantep, recipe brought from Damascus.
t.tech: thin filo layers with pistachio, baked and soaked in syrup
t.auth: Turkish GI 2008; EU PGI 2013

t.d: Fermenting and ageing wine with skins, stalks and pips in large buried egg-shaped clay jars.
t.tech: whole-grape fermentation in sealed buried qvevri for 5–6 months or more; vessels lime-washed and beeswaxed
t.auth: label names qvevri/kvevri; long skin contact gives amber colour and tannin in whites

t.d: Sausage-making with more than 1,500 types, mostly in natural casings, with strict composition rules since the 13th century.
t.tech: Raw, cooked and smoked sausage making.

t.d: Making and sharing kimchi for winter over about a month from the tenth lunar month, inscribed by UNESCO in 2013.
t.tech: salting and fermenting vegetables, once in earthenware jars buried in the ground
t.auth: Practice inscribed, not kimchi itself; North Korea's tradition inscribed separately in 2015

t.d: Brewing method using small pots and many short infusions of a large leaf quantity.
t.tech: short infusions of 10-15 seconds lengthening each pour
t.mat: Yixing clay teapot or gaiwan, thin porcelain cups, fairness cup
t.auth: Small vessels, repeated infusions, rinsing of pot and leaf

t.d: Syrup waffles first baked in Gouda and still made there by bakeries and factories.
t.tech: thin waffle baked on an iron, split and filled with syrup

t.d: Turin breadsticks in the hand-rolled rubatà and stretched stirato forms.
t.tech: hand-rolling (rubatà) or stretching (stirato)
t.mat: wheat flour, water, yeast, olive oil
t.auth: Rubatà show an irregular knobby hand-rolled surface and run 40–80 cm.

t.d: Artisan cane spirit made by some 500–600 village micro-distilleries (guildives).
t.tech: Spontaneous fermentation of cane juice or syrup; distillation in Creole stills; no filtration
t.auth: HaïRum certification mark

t.r: Balkans, Middle East, Central and South Asia
t.d: Seed-paste and flour-based halvas made across a wide region.
t.tech: seed paste or roasted flour cooked with sugar and fat; floss types pulled
t.mat: sesame tahini, sunflower seed, flour, sugar, ghee

t.r: Nepal, Bhutan, Tibet and Northeast India
t.d: Mountain cheesemaking from yak and cow buttermilk, producing soft fresh chhurpi and fire-dried hard chewing cheese.
t.tech: Buttermilk boiled, curd drained in cloth, pressed in jute bags, cut into cubes and dried over a fire
t.auth: Hard chhurpi is extremely hard and lasts 30 minutes to five hours in the mouth; soft chhurpi is white and mild.

t.d: Strong 'silk-stocking' black tea with evaporated milk, sold fresh and as cold milk tea in cans and bottles.
t.tech: Ceylon black tea blend mixed with evaporated or condensed milk
forms: canned or bottled cold milk tea
t.auth: smooth, strong tea with evaporated milk; technique listed as Hong Kong intangible cultural heritage (2017)

t.r: Spain and Portugal (Huelva, Córdoba, Cáceres, Badajoz, Salamanca, Alentejo)
t.d: Dry-curing of hind legs from black Iberian pigs reared on dehesa oak pasture.
t.tech: Final fattening on acorns and grass; cured for months to years.
t.auth: Four PDOs; since 2014 coloured labels: black (100% ibérico de bellota, the only pata negra), red, green and white.

t.r: Portugal and western Spain (Beira, Alentejo, Extremadura)
t.d: Raw ewe's-milk cheeses coagulated with cardoon (Cynara cardunculus) flowers instead of animal rennet, ripened to a soft paste.
t.tech: thistle-flower coagulation, slow draining, cloth binding
t.mat: raw sheep's milk, cardoon pistils, salt
t.auth: PDO label and regulatory council seal; raw milk; slightly bitter note from thistle

t.d: Ghee made by culturing boiled milk into curd, churning out the butter and simmering it until the solids brown.
t.tech: milk set to curd (dahi), churned in a wooden bilona to separate makhan from chaas, butter slowly heated and strained
t.mat: cow or water-buffalo milk, curd starter
t.auth: ingredient list of milk or butter only; nutty, caramel aroma; cream-based ghee skips the curd step

t.d: Mango cultivation and ritual in South Asia, with groves valued by Ashoka, the Mughals and in worship.
t.tech: grafting of monoembryonic cultivars such as Alphonso and Langra
t.auth: Named grafted cultivars; GI marks for several

t.d: Clove-and-tobacco cigarettes first made in Kudus, credited to Hajj Djamhari, first sold as medicine.
t.tech: Tobacco blended with minced dried clove buds, hand-rolled or machine-made
t.auth: Crackling sound when burning; sold by named Indonesian makers.

t.d: Artisanal Italian ice cream tradition of low-fat, low-air gelato made daily in gelaterie.
t.tech: custard or milk base pasteurised, batch-frozen with little air
t.auth: 6–9% butterfat, 20–35% air, served softer than ice cream

t.d: Italian meat products, mostly cured pork, served as antipasto; the name comes from Latin sal, salt.
t.tech: Salting and curing; some, such as mortadella, are cooked.
t.auth: Some are PDO (prosciutto di Parma, San Daniele); others such as Salame Felino hold the Italian traditional agri-food product (PAT) status.

t.d: Regional Italian nougats eaten at Christmas.
t.tech: egg white, sugar and honey whipped and set with nuts
t.auth: Torrone di Bagnara holds the Italian IGP

t.d: Local chickens whose parents, or one parent, are native to Japan, raised by a prescribed method.
t.tech: Slow rearing at low stocking density.

t.d: Seed-koji merchants who keep, cultivate and sell koji mould spores to sake, miso and soy-sauce makers.
t.tech: koji mould grown on steamed rice with wood ash, spores sold on grain or as powder
t.mat: Aspergillus oryzae and related moulds; rice, barley
t.auth: about ten moyashiya remain in Japan; strains are chosen per product (sake, miso, shōchū)

t.d: Japanese tofu styles from silken kinugoshi and pressed momen to fried, frozen and freeze-dried forms.
t.tech: gypsum-set unpressed (kinugoshi) or pressed (momen) curd; deep-frying; freezing and freeze-drying

t.d: Fermenting soybeans with Rhizopus mould into a bound cake; said to have begun in Bayat, Klaten, Central Java. Indonesia submitted it to UNESCO's intangible heritage list in March 2024 (pending).
t.tech: soaking, dehulling and boiling beans, inoculating with Rhizopus and incubating in leaves or plastic
t.mat: soybeans, Rhizopus oligosporus or R. oryzae, teak or waru leaves

t.d: Black tea grown largely on smallholdings through the Kenya Tea Development Agency and sold at the Mombasa auction.
t.tech: crush-tear-curl (CTC) processing, plus orthodox whole leaf
t.auth: Sold by auction lot and factory; no single certification mark named

t.d: Hard white charcoal from ubame oak, prized for long, clean, hot burning in Japanese grilling.
t.tech: Slow kiln pyrolysis (about 240 °C for 120 hours), then about 1,000 °C, cured in damp earth, sand and ash
t.auth: Wakayama Prefectural Charcoal Cooperative yellow label; regional collective trademark since 2006; metallic ring when struck

t.d: Making, keeping and eating jang, the fermented sauces including soybean paste, soy sauce and red chilli paste.
t.tech: meju bricks fermented, brine drawn as ganjang, remainder mashed as doenjang
t.auth: Family transmission, mother to daughter, in earthenware jars

t.p: Three Kingdoms to present; revived after 1990s
t.d: Home and regional brewing of rice wines and spirits with nuruk starters, suppressed under colonial rule and grain laws.
t.tech: Multi-stage fermentation of steamed rice with nuruk; clear cheongju drawn off, cloudy takju kept unfiltered
t.mat: Rice, glutinous rice, wheat nuruk, water, flowers and herbs
t.auth: Designated intangible-heritage recipes (e.g. No. 86-2, 86-3); traditional nuruk rather than manufactured starter

t.d: Unchurned frozen dessert of slow-reduced milk, sold by kulfiwallahs.
t.tech: milk reduced and caramelised, frozen in sealed moulds in a matka of ice and salt
ctr: Kuremal Mohan Lal Kulfi Wale, Old Delhi (1906)
t.auth: dense, slow-melting, no ice crystals, cooked-milk taste

t.p: first recorded 988; commercial from the late 19th century
t.d: Low-alcohol rye bread or malt drink brewed at home and sold from street barrels and bottles.
t.tech: rye bread or malt soaked in hot water, short fermentation with yeast and lactic bacteria
t.mat: rye bread, rye malt, sugar, yeast, berries or herbs
t.auth: fermented from bread or malt, under about 1.2–1.5% alcohol; unfermented malt-extract drinks are kvass-style beverages

t.p: pre-Meiji (before 1868); name adopted 1960; brand certification from 1989
t.d: Heirloom vegetables of Kyoto, certified as brand products and tied to kaiseki and temple cooking.
t.tech: local seed selection, small-lot farming
t.auth: Kyoto Prefecture brand-product certification

t.d: Top-fermented, cold-conditioned pale ale brewed only within 50 km of Cologne under the Kölsch-Konvention.
t.tech: warm top fermentation then cold conditioning
t.mat: pale malt, some wheat allowed, hops
t.auth: Brewed by a Konvention signatory within 50 km of Cologne; served in the Stange.

t.r: Armenia, Iran, Azerbaijan, Turkey, Central Asia
t.d: Thin flatbread slapped on the walls of a tonir clay oven; UNESCO-listed for Armenia (2014) and multinationally (2016).
t.tech: Dough stretched thin and baked 15–40 seconds on tonir walls

t.d: Grape-and-aniseed spirit of the Levant, centred on Zahlé and the Bekaa Valley.
t.tech: Grapes fermented about three weeks, distilled, redistilled with aniseed, then a slow third distillation; aged in clay amphorae
t.auth: Quality arak is triple distilled and amphora-aged, typically about 53% ABV.

t.d: Limbu drink of fermented finger millet served to honour guests and shared by newlyweds under the Mundhum.
t.tech: Cooked millet fermented with marchā starter, steeped in hot water, sipped through a filtering bamboo straw
t.mat: Finger millet, marchā, bamboo, wood or brass vessel
t.auth: Served as moist fermented millet in a tongba vessel topped up with hot water.

t.d: Skrei hung to dry outdoors for about three months, Norway's oldest food export still traded.
t.tech: open-air racks, cold wind, then sorting into 20-plus grades
t.auth: Tørrfisk fra Lofoten PGI

t.d: Starch-and-sugar gel confection of Ottoman tradition.
t.tech: starch and sugar cooked to a gel, set, cut into cubes and dusted
t.auth: Loukoumi Geroskipou carries the Cyprus PGI

t.d: High-almond marzipan of the former Hanseatic hub.
t.tech: almond paste worked with limited sugar and moulded or coated
t.auth: PGI since 1996: at most 30% sugar, Fine at most 10%

t.r: Maghreb: Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Mauritania
t.d: Gunpowder green tea brewed with fresh spearmint and sugar, poured from a height.
t.tech: boiling water, leaves left in the pot, high pour
t.auth: Served at least three glasses; flavour changes glass to glass

t.d: Turkish mastic ice cream thickened with salep.
t.tech: pounded and stretched rather than churned
t.auth: chewy, elastic, slow to melt

t.d: Finishing oysters in shallow clay ponds left from old salt marshes, where Blue Navicula algae colours the gills green.
t.tech: affinage in claires, 28 days up to 8 months
t.mat: clay ponds, tidal fresh and salt water
t.auth: PGI and Label Rouge labels

t.d: Candied chestnuts made by a near twenty-step process.
t.tech: chestnuts candied in syrup over days and glazed, much by hand

t.p: traditional; now mostly a soft drink
t.d: Bittersweet bark drink, once fermented in small batches, now often syrup or soda.
t.tech: bark and spices boiled, bottled and sun-warmed, fermented up to a week with a previous batch
t.mat: Colubrina bark, cinnamon, cloves, aniseed, orange peel, brown sugar
t.auth: bitter bark taste; fermented versions foam

t.d: Toledo marzipan with protected status.
t.tech: almonds and sugar kneaded and shaped
t.auth: PGI: almonds at least 50% by weight

t.d: Fresh-fruit ice pops, milk- or water-based, made by paleterías and sold by paleteros.
t.tech: fresh fruit frozen on a stick
t.auth: fresh-fruit base; local flavours such as tamarind, mamey, horchata

t.d: Fermented maguey sap drink sold in pulquerías.
t.tech: Aguamiel tapped twice daily and fermented 7–14 days with seed pulque (Zymomonas mobilis)
t.auth: Fresh, viscous, milky; canning changes the flavour

t.r: Oaxaca and other DO states, Mexico
t.d: Village palenque mezcal making from cultivated and wild agaves.
t.tech: Pit-roasting agave, milling by mallet or stone tahona, fermenting, distilling in copper, clay or wood stills
t.mat: Agave (espadín, tobalá and other wild species)
t.auth: Certified category on label (mezcal, artesanal, ancestral), agave species and producer named

t.d: Milk, flour and nut sweets made by halwai shops for festivals and gifts.
t.tech: milk reduced to khoya or curdled to chhena, flour roasted in ghee, sugar syrup
t.mat: milk, chhena, gram flour, ghee, nuts, silver leaf
t.auth: GI tags: Banglar Rasogolla (2017), Odisha Rasagola (2019)

t.p: from 1330; rise from the Kan'ei period (17th century)
t.d: Five brewing districts producing about a quarter of Japan's sake, known for strong, full sake.
t.tech: Tanba tōji brewmasters; cold Rokkō oroshi winds slow fermentation
t.mat: Miyamizu hard water from Mount Rokkō; Yamada Nishiki rice
t.auth: Nada-Gogō geographical indication on the label

t.d: Portuguese-derived sponge cake regarded as wagashi.
t.tech: baked in square moulds with mizuame and zarame

t.p: Traditional; Ordine del Nocino Modenese since 1978
t.d: Walnut liqueur of green walnuts steeped in spirit and sweetened, a household and artisan tradition around Modena.
t.tech: Unripe walnuts picked around St John's Day (24 June), steeped in alcohol, mixed with syrup and aged
t.auth: Dark brown colour; traditional harvest around 24 June

t.d: Liquorice flavoured with ammonium chloride (salmiak), from mild to double salt.
t.tech: liquorice mass flavoured or dusted with salmiak salt
t.mat: liquorice extract, ammonium chloride, sugar, starch
t.auth: salmiak listed in ingredients; dubbelzout marks double salt

t.d: Room-temperature fermented milks of the Nordic countries, from thick filmjölk to ropy viili and drinkable piimä.
t.tech: Mesophilic fermentation with Lactococcus lactis and Leuconostoc; Geotrichum candidum on viili
t.auth: Mesophilic cultures give a mild, buttery sourness; viili has a velvety mould surface

t.d: Mesophilic ropy fermented milks set at room temperature.
t.tech: mesophilic lactic fermentation with surface Geotrichum candidum
t.auth: long, ropy texture and velvety mould surface

t.p: Whey spreads for at least 2,500 years; firm cream brunost from 1863
t.d: Boiling whey, with milk or cream, until the milk sugars caramelise into brown whey cheese or spread.
t.tech: Whey reduced about 10:1 in iron pots; cream added for the firm modern cheese
t.mat: Cow's and goat's whey, milk and cream
t.auth: Ekte geitost contains no cow's milk; Gudbrandsdalsost mixes cow's and goat's milk

t.r: Western Norway (Hordaland, Sogn og Fjordane, Møre og Romsdal)
t.d: Farm brewing of juniper-infused ale with each farm's own kveik yeast, passed down in families.
t.tech: juniper infusion, long boil or raw ale, warm fermentation of about 48 hours
t.auth: kveik kept on yeast rings, wooden logs or as dried flakes; strains named for farm or brewer

t.d: White honey-and-almond nougat of Montélimar.
t.tech: whipped egg white with lavender honey and sugar, set with roasted nuts
t.mat: lavender honey, almonds, pistachios, egg white
t.auth: protected status since 2024

t.d: Guild-baked honey-spice cakes, protected since 1996.
t.tech: nut-rich dough baked on wafer
t.auth: made within the city; Elisen grade ≥25% nuts, <10% flour

t.r: West Africa, South and Southeast Asia, Pacific, western Mexico
t.d: Tapping palm flower stalks for sap that ferments naturally within hours.
t.tech: Flower stalk cut and sap collected in a fastened container; wild-yeast fermentation
t.mat: Coconut, palmyra, oil, raffia, date, nipa or kaong palm sap
t.auth: Sold fresh; sours within a day

t.d: Raw dry-cured hind leg made under EU protected designation of origin in two named zones.
t.tech: Salted in stages, rested, then hung in humidity-controlled rooms; aged at least 14 months.
t.mat: Pig hind leg and sea salt only; no nitrites or nitrates for Parma.
t.auth: Consorzio del Prosciutto di Parma brands each ham with the ducal crown after a horse-bone needle check; the word prosciutto alone is not protected.

t.d: Dry pasta made in Gragnano from durum semolina and Lattari mountain water.
t.tech: bronze-die extrusion, slow drying at 40-80 C
t.auth: IGP mark; produced and packed in Gragnano

t.d: Persian water pipe, with literary reference by Ahlī Shirazi before 1535 and a court post of hookah tender.
t.tech: Water pipe smoking
t.mat: Glass and precious metals for the rich

t.d: Mountain blue cheeses of cow's or mixed milks matured in natural limestone caves and once wrapped in leaves.
t.tech: Natural cave ripening at about 90% humidity and 7–13 °C
t.mat: Raw cow's milk, often blended with goat and sheep milk
t.auth: PDO or PGI stamp on the wrapper; Cabrales in dark green foil.

t.d: Pastoral Pokot method of fermenting raw milk in smoked gourds and finishing it with tree ash.
t.tech: raw milk kept at least three days in gourds smoked over kromwo wood, whey drained, shaken, ash added
t.mat: goat's or cow's milk, gourd calabashes, kromwo (Ozoroa insignis) ash
t.auth: light grey colour and aromatic, resinous note from the ash

t.d: Regional sausages smoked or fresh, of pork, beef, veal or turkey, with dozens of varieties.
t.tech: Smoking, air-drying, scalding.
t.auth: EU PGI for kiełbasa lisiecka, kiełbasa biała parzona wielkopolska and kiełbasa piaszczańska; TSG for kabanosy staropolskie, krakowska sucha staropolska and others.

t.p: Medieval–present; grade names 17th–18th c.; EU TSG 2008
t.d: Mead made in four legally defined grades by honey-to-water ratio and ageing.
t.tech: Honey must fermented and aged 9 months to 3 years
t.mat: Honey, water, sometimes fruit juice or spices
t.auth: TSG label with grade name; ratio and minimum ageing per grade

t.d: Liquorice discs from a town where liquorice was grown, stamped with the castle.
t.tech: liquorice paste sweetened and stamped into small discs
t.auth: small black discs about 19 mm across with a castle stamp

t.d: Hand-prepared tinned sardines, tuna and mackerel in olive oil, with aged vintage tins valued like wine.
t.tech: fish cut and gutted by hand, steamed outside the can, packed in tinplate and aged at least six months
t.mat: sardines, tuna, carapau, cod, octopus, olive oil, tinplate
t.auth: look for aged reserve tins and ANICP member producers

t.d: Yunnan large-leaf tea compressed and aged, in raw (sheng) and wet-piled ripe (shou) styles.
t.tech: sun-drying, compression, natural ageing or wet piling (since 1973)
t.auth: Four-digit factory recipe numbers; 2008 standard limits the name to Yunnan tea

t.d: Hungarian fruit brandy distilled only from Hungarian-grown fruit, protected in the EU since 2004 and by the 2008 pálinka law.
t.tech: Whole-fruit mash fermentation; double distillation in small copper pot stills (kisüsti) or single column distillation
t.mat: Plums, apricots, apples, pears, cherries, sour cherries, quince, grape pomace
t.auth: Hungarian fruit and production, no additives beyond fruit, at least 37.5% ABV, registered distillery; regional PDO name where claimed.

t.d: Baltic sprats smoked on alder and canned in oil under a producers' logo.
t.tech: alder smoking then canning in oil
t.auth: the Riga Sprats in Oil logo of the member association

t.d: Industrial and artisan alfajores filled with dulce de leche.
t.tech: biscuits sandwiched with dulce de leche, coated in chocolate or sugar
t.mat: flour or cornstarch, dulce de leche, chocolate

t.d: Ripening of Lacaune ewe's-milk blue cheese in the natural Combalou caves, the only place where Roquefort may be aged.
t.tech: Cave ageing with Penicillium roqueforti
t.auth: Roquefort PDO name and aging in the Combalou caves.

t.d: Salt-curing of spring-caught Cantabrian anchovies for at least six months before filleting and packing in olive oil.
t.tech: clean, salt, cure six months or more, wash, fillet by hand, pack in olive oil
t.auth: fillets firm but flexible, 9 to 12 cm, only anchovies, olive oil and salt; kept chilled

t.d: Rye hard bread baked in thin rounds with a central hole and dried on poles.
t.tech: thin-rolled rye dough baked dry, often sourdough
t.auth: Rye-based, very low moisture, traditional round form with hole.

t.p: Ancient; spread nationally in the late Qing
t.d: Glutinous-rice huangjiu brewing with wheat qu, aged in earthenware jars and dated by brewing year.
t.tech: Fermentation with wheat-based qu; jar ageing for years or decades
t.mat: Glutinous rice, wheat qu, local water
t.auth: Wine from outside Shaoxing labelled as Shaoxing is a common fraud

t.r: Iran, Turkey, Arab world, South Asia
t.p: Medieval Persian origin; Mughal India from 16th century
t.d: Sweet fruit, flower and herb syrups diluted with water, popular at Ramadan iftar.
t.tech: Fruit juice, petals or essences boiled with sugar into syrup; Ottoman crystallised tablets
t.mat: rose, sandalwood, bael, khus, lemon, pomegranate, tamarind, sugar

t.d: Fruit infused in vinegar, sweetened and reduced to a syrup for mixing with water or soda.
t.tech: Vinegar infusion of fruit, strained, sweetened and reduced

t.d: Natural brewing of soy sauce in handmade cedar-and-bamboo kioke barrels, about 1% of Japan's soy sauce.
t.tech: Tennen Jōzō Kioke Shikomi: natural wooden-barrel fermentation
t.mat: cedar and bamboo barrels, soybean, wheat, salt
t.auth: Brewed in kioke barrels; barrels can last over 100 years

t.d: Yuasa claims to be the birthplace of Japanese soy sauce, with a soy sauce industry flourishing since the Edo period.
t.tech: koji fermentation of soybean and wheat with brine, pressed and aged
t.auth: Claim of origin is local and not settled

t.d: Pastoral method of ripening salted, crumbled curd packed into a cleaned animal skin stored in caves or cellars.
t.tech: Curd drained, brined, kneaded with raw milk and packed tightly into a salted skin, then cellar-ripened for months
t.mat: Goat's or sheep's milk; goat, sheep or calf skin
t.auth: Ripened in real skin rather than plastic barrels; regional geographical-indication names such as Erzincan tulum.

t.d: Farmhouse cheddar made from the farm's own raw milk, cheddared by hand, bound in cloth and aged at least a year.
t.tech: cheddaring by hand, cloth binding, long cellar ageing
t.mat: raw cow's milk, rennet, cloth, lard
t.auth: Raw milk, cloth-bound natural rind, maker's farm name; Slow Food presidium members.

t.d: Thick sour milk of Zulu, Xhosa, Ndebele, Swazi and Sotho tradition, eaten over maize porridge.
t.tech: Unpasteurised milk fermented one to five days in a smoked calabash or hide sack, whey drained
t.auth: Traditional amasi is calabash-fermented raw milk; commercial versions use Lactococcus lactis on pasteurised milk

t.d: Knotted soft pretzels dipped in lye before baking.
t.tech: dough twisted into the pretzel loop, dipped in lye or washing soda, salted and baked
t.auth: Bavarian: thick arms, little fat; Swabian: thin arms, split fat belly

t.d: Stuffed and cured sausages; the Royal Spanish Academy defines embutido as intestine stuffed with minced meat, mainly pork.
t.tech: Stuffing into casings, then curing.
t.mat: Pork, sometimes blood and other fillings.

t.d: Christmas almond-and-honey turrón of Jijona, Alicante and Agramunt.
t.tech: almonds with honey, sugar and egg white, ground to paste (Jijona) or left whole (Alicante)
t.auth: PGI labels; about 64% almonds (Jijona) and 60% (Alicante)

t.d: Spirit distilled from fermented sap of unopened coconut flowers.
t.tech: Sap tapping, fermentation, distillation; ageing in halmilla wood vats
t.auth: Only coconut sap and water in premium grades; common grades blended with molasses or neutral spirit

t.d: Baltic herring brined then canned to ferment further, sold from the third Thursday of August.
t.tech: caught May and June, brined, headed and gutted, barrelled at 15 to 18 C, canned early July
t.auth: sale date and tin fermentation

t.d: Aged hard cheese with many small irregular holes, a style unique to Sweden.
t.tech: Curd salted in the mass rather than brined; long cellar ageing; waxed wheels
t.auth: Svecia PGI mark; made in Sweden from Swedish milk

t.d: Moist steam-pasteurised tobacco placed under the upper lip, shifting from nasal snuff to snus by the early 1800s.
t.tech: Steam pasteurisation rather than fermentation; loose or portion
t.auth: Sold in Sweden under the EU exemption; most other EU sales of tobacco snus are banned.

t.r: Swiss Alps, Jura massif, Savoie, Allgäu, Vorarlberg and Tyrol
t.d: Large cooked-pressed cheeses from raw cow's milk made in village co-operatives and summer Alp huts, then aged for months.
t.tech: curd cooked in copper cauldrons, sometimes over wood fire, pressed into large wheels, brined and cellar-aged with turning and brushing
t.mat: raw cow's milk from pasture or hay, no silage
t.auth: AOP/PDO marks, casein or rind marks, Comté green or brown band, Appenzeller colour labels

t.d: Salty soy-glazed rice crackers popularised from a Sōka teahouse.
t.tech: rice crackers baked and brushed with soy sauce

t.d: Oolong grown above 1,000 m in Nantou and Chiayi, hand-harvested at low yield.
t.tech: hand harvest, tarp withering, bruising, oxidation over about 36-40 hours
t.auth: Sweet, milky, floral cup; the source names no certification

t.d: Quick street-vendor ferment of pineapple peel, once made from maize.
t.tech: wild fermentation of peel with sugar for one to two days, sometimes in barrels
t.mat: pineapple peel and rind, piloncillo, cinnamon, chilli
t.auth: slight fizz and tartness from live fermentation; sold chilled

t.r: Valles region, Jalisco, Mexico (Tequila, Amatitán, El Arenal, Magdalena)
t.d: Blue-agave cultivation and tequila distilling, recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape in 2006.
t.tech: Cooking, fermenting and distilling blue agave hearts
t.auth: NOM distillery number and Tequila Regulatory Council certification; '100% agave' on the label

t.d: Botrytised aszú berries macerated in must and cask-aged; vineyards classified from 1730 in one of the first appellations.
t.tech: Hand-picking aszú berries, paste maceration, cask ageing; puttonyos grading
t.auth: Tokaji designation; puttonyos and vintage on label

t.d: Traditional Polish gingerbread of Toruń.
t.tech: moulded spiced honey dough

t.r: Pajottenland and Senne valley, south-west of Brussels (Belgium)
t.p: 13th century to present; gueuze EU TSG 1997/98
t.d: Spontaneously fermented wheat beer, aged in wood and blended into gueuze or refermented on fruit, guarded by the High Council for Artisanal Lambic Beers (HORAL).
t.tech: Wort cooled overnight in an open coolship, inoculated by airborne yeasts and bacteria, brewed October to May, aged in barrels with old dry hops, blended young with old
t.mat: Barley malt, unmalted wheat, aged hops, oak barrels, whole fruit (Schaarbeek cherries, raspberries)
t.auth: 'Oude Gueuze'/'Oude Geuze' and 'Oude Kriek' on the label mean unsweetened blends of 100% lambic; HORAL contested 'Méthode Gueuze' abroad (Jester King now uses 'Méthode Traditionnelle').

t.d: Japanese vegetable pickling in salt, brine or a fermented rice-bran bed, using tubs, pressing stones and screw-top pickle presses.
t.tech: Vegetables pressed under weight in salt or buried in a daily-stirred rice-bran (nuka) bed.
t.mat: Wooden or ceramic tubs, enamel or plastic nukadoko containers, pickle presses
t.auth: Traditional nukadoko is kept alive by daily hand-stirring; pressing containers are judged by lid pressure and capacity rather than brand.

t.d: Turin chocolate-making that blends chocolate with hazelnut paste, giving the gianduiotto and cremino.
t.tech: chocolate blended with about 30% hazelnut paste
t.auth: ingot shape and hazelnut share

t.r: Turkey and the former Ottoman lands
t.d: Very fine coffee boiled unfiltered with grounds left in the cup; on UNESCO's intangible heritage list.
t.tech: brought to the boil up to three times in a cezve
t.mat: Medium-roast arabica, copper cezve, thin porcelain cups
t.auth: Fine powder grind, cezve, thick froth, water served first

t.d: Preparation of very finely ground coffee boiled unfiltered in a cezve, inscribed by UNESCO in 2013.
t.tech: slow heating of coffee and water in a long-handled pot until it foams, served with grounds settling
t.mat: hammered copper or brass, tinned; silver; later steel and ceramic
t.auth: hand-hammered marks, tinned interior, riveted long handle; capacity sized in cups

t.d: Turkish water pipe tradition, nargile.
t.tech: Water pipe smoking

t.p: Tea planted from the late 12th century; sencha 1738
t.d: Japanese shaded and steamed green tea from Uji and neighbouring Kyoto areas.
t.tech: ōishita shading with straw or reed covers; steaming, rolling, kneading
t.auth: A regional name needs all-local leaf; many farmers still hand-process

t.d: Birthplace of commercial absinthe: Dubied and Pernod at Couvet, then Pernod Fils at Pontarlier; revived at Môtiers after legalisation.
t.tech: Maceration of wormwood, anise and fennel in alcohol, redistilled; verte gets a second herbal maceration for colour
t.mat: Grand wormwood, green anise, fennel, wine or neutral alcohol
t.auth: Swiss court ruled in 2014 that 'absinthe' is a product name, not a protected origin; look for named Val-de-Travers or Pontarlier distilleries.

t.d: Seasonal Japanese confectionery served with green tea.
t.tech: bean paste, rice and agar cooked, moulded or steamed; graded by moisture
t.mat: azuki, rice, mochi, agar, wasanbon sugar

t.d: Partly oxidised cliff-grown tea from the Wuyi Mountains, made by withering, shaking, rolling, firing and baking.
t.tech: withering, making (shaking and rolling), stir-frying, kneading, baking
t.mat: Wuyi cultivars (Da Hong Pao, Rou Gui, Shui Xian, Tie Luo Han, Bai Jiguan)
t.auth: Mother-tree Da Hong Pao is rare; most market tea is from cuttings

t.d: Home brewing of maize and sorghum beer for initiation homecomings, weddings, funerals and calling the ancestors.
t.tech: Mash of maize meal and maize and sorghum malt fermented overnight in a potjie, strained, sediment returned
t.mat: Maize meal, maize malt, sorghum malt, water
t.auth: Thick, sour, opaque buff-coloured brew under 3% alcohol, made in a cast-iron pot.

t.r: Rhubarb Triangle, West Yorkshire, England (Wakefield, Morley, Rothwell)
t.d: Rhubarb crowns grown two years in the field, then forced in heated dark sheds and picked by candlelight.
t.tech: field-grown roots frosted, moved into heated windowless sheds in November, harvested by candlelight
t.auth: 'Yorkshire Forced Rhubarb' carries EU Protected Designation of Origin (2010).

t.d: Damson plum brandy; Serbia’s traditional šljivovica-making was inscribed on UNESCO’s intangible heritage list in 2022.
t.tech: Fermentation of lightly pressed plums with kernels intact; one or more distillations; often oak-aged
t.auth: Protected national names (Srpska šljivovica, Troyanska slivova, Tetevenska slivova); damson plum base.

t.d: Wearing of dehn al oud, Taif rose oil, musk and blended mukhallat oils, traded by family houses in Gulf souqs.
t.tech: agarwood oil distillation; copper-pot distillation of Taif rose sold by the tola; blending into mukhallat
t.mat: agarwood (Aquilaria), Taif damask rose, white musk, amber, saffron
t.auth: origin and wood species stated; wild vs cultivated agarwood; natural oud oil yields are tiny, so cheap 'pure' oils are suspect

t.d: Hydro-distillation of flowers, herbs and baked earth into a sandalwood base in copper stills; Kannauj perfumes hold a GI tag (2014).
t.tech: deg (copper still) sealed with clay, bamboo pipe to a bhapka of sandalwood oil, wood and cow-dung fire, repeated charges
t.mat: damask rose, jasmine, vetiver, kewra, baked clay, spices; sandalwood oil or liquid paraffin
t.auth: Kannauj GI tag; sandalwood rather than paraffin base; no alcohol; maker's distillery named

t.d: Kiln production of hard white charcoal from ubame oak, designated an intangible folk cultural property of Wakayama in 1974.
t.tech: Slow kiln pyrolysis (about 240 °C for 120 hours), final firing near 1,000 °C, then smothering in damp earth, sand and ash
t.auth: Yellow label of the Wakayama Prefectural Charcoal Cooperative; Regional Collective Trademark (2006); metallic ring when struck

t.d: Japanese hydration-first skin care, with the cleansing oil (Shu Uemura, 1960) and keshōsui lotion pressed into the skin after cleansing.
t.tech: Oil cleanse, then keshōsui pressed in by hand in layers rather than wiped on, then milk or cream.
t.mat: cleansing oils, hyaluronic and rice- or sake-based lotions
t.auth: Japanese-market packaging with Japanese ingredient labels; to verify per product.

t.d: Korean multi-step skin-care regimen that went global from 2011, beginning with the double cleanse.
t.tech: Double cleanse: oil-based cleanser to melt make-up and sunscreen, then a water-based cleanser; then toner, essence, serum, sheet mask, moisturiser, sunscreen.
t.mat: cleansing oils and balms, low-pH gel and foam cleansers, essences, sheet masks
t.auth: Korean labelling and authorised sellers; counterfeit risk to verify per brand.

t.d: Cleaning the teeth with a chewed twig: the miswak of Salvadora persica in the Islamic world, neem datun in India and chew sticks across Africa.
t.tech: The end of a fresh twig is chewed until its fibres splay into a brush; used before prayer in Islamic practice.
t.mat: Salvadora persica (arak, 'toothbrush tree'); neem; banyan and other local trees
t.auth: True miswak is cut from Salvadora persica; other woods are sold as generic chew sticks.

t.d: London barbers' and perfumers' tradition of the hot-towel shave and brush-lathered soaps and creams.
t.tech: hot-towel wet shave; brush lathering of soap or cream
t.mat: shaving soap and cream, badger brushes, razors
t.auth: house name and royal warrant on product and shop

t.d: Italian barbershop tradition of pre- and after-shave creams used by barbers first, then home shavers.
t.tech: barbershop wet shave with pre-shave cream
ctr: Martelli family, Florence (Proraso; firm 1908, pre-shave cream 1948)
t.auth: family firm branding

t.d: London barbershops that sell their own shaving creams, soaps and colognes, several holding Royal Warrants.
t.tech: barbering; in-house shaving creams and fragrances
t.auth: shop name and Royal Warrant marks on packaging

t.p: Ancient; in use since about 1900 BC
t.d: Hair removal with a cooked sugar paste, known as sukkar or ḥalawa in the Middle East, ağda in Turkey and moum in Iran.
t.tech: Paste of sugar, lemon juice and water applied by hand or spatula and flicked off, or used with cloth strips
t.mat: sugar, lemon juice, water; historically honey
t.auth: True sugar paste is water-soluble and resin-free; many shop products add wax.

t.r: India and Iran; spread to Europe and North America
t.p: Traditional; in the West from the 1980s
t.d: Hair removal with a doubled, twisted cotton or polyester thread rolled over the skin, mostly for shaping eyebrows.
t.tech: Twisted thread worked by hand, mouth or neck method

t.p: Classical texts from the first centuries CE; mineral preparations (rasashastra) after the 11th century
t.d: South Asian healing tradition whose preparations are mostly plant-based; listed here for forms and registration only.
t.tech: Herbal compounding; rasashastra adds metals and minerals after purification (shodhana)
t.mat: Mostly plants; also metals, minerals, oils and fats
ctr: Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences
t.auth: Indian products must state metallic content; voluntary Ayush Standard Mark (Schedule T GMP) and Ayush Premium Mark (WHO GMP) run by the Quality Council of India since 2009.

t.d: System of highly diluted preparations devised by Samuel Hahnemann; listed here for forms and registration only.
t.tech: Serial dilution on C, D/X or Q scales; drops placed on lactose pills
t.auth: UK Simplified Registration products carry no indications; UK National Rules products may name minor conditions and say 'UK Only'; the US FDA has approved no homeopathic product.

t.p: Chinese medicine arrived in the 6th century; extract granules from the 1920s; NHI reimbursement from 1967
t.d: Japanese adaptation of Chinese herbal medicine using fixed formulas in standard proportions; listed here for forms and registration only.
t.tech: Fixed formulas made into dried decoction extract granules
t.mat: Crude herbal drugs listed in the Japanese Pharmacopoeia
ctr: Keio University Center for Kampo Medicine
t.auth: 148 formula extracts approved by Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, each with the same ingredients whichever maker.

t.p: Han dynasty classics (1st c. BCE onward); modern system standardised in the PRC from the 1950s
t.d: Chinese healing tradition whose ready-made products are sold as patent medicines; listed here for forms and registration only.
t.tech: Herbal formulas made into pills, powders, pastes, extract granules and external plasters
t.mat: Plant, animal, fungal and mineral materials
t.auth: Mainland products follow Chinese Pharmacopoeia Vol. 1 monographs; Hong Kong proprietary Chinese medicines carry a registration number HKC-XXXXX; Tong Ren Tang products are often counterfeited.

t.r: South and Central Asia, chiefly India and Pakistan
t.p: Greco-Arabic, from Avicenna's Canon of Medicine; in India from the 12th century
t.d: Greco-Arabic humoral healing tradition practised in South Asia; listed here for forms and registration only.
t.tech: Herbal medicines compounded by hakims, with regimental therapies
ctr: Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine
t.auth: Regulated in India under the Ministry of Ayush and in Pakistan by the National Council for Tibb; Indian Unani products can carry the voluntary Ayush Mark.

t.r: Arabian Peninsula, Gulf and wider Muslim world
t.d: Burning scented chips, pastilles and agarwood in a mabkhara to perfume homes and welcome guests.
t.tech: Indirect burning on charcoal in a censer
t.auth: Real agarwood is dense, dark and resinous; adulteration and plantation wood are common

t.p: Ancient; bamboo-core stick from the late 19th century
t.d: Indian stick incense made from a paste on bamboo, scented with masala or perfume oils.
t.tech: Hand-rolled masala paste on bamboo; dhoop rolled or extruded without a core
t.mat: Charcoal or sawdust, jiggit binder, halmaddi resin, sandalwood
t.auth: Hand-rolled masala texture versus dipped charcoal sticks

t.p: Late Muromachi period (16th century) to present
t.d: Japanese incense-appreciation tradition whose utensils, incense woods and boxes are collected as objects; the practice itself belongs to the pursuit taxonomy.
t.tech: Agarwood slivers heated on a mica plate over ash in a censer; incense-guessing games
t.mat: Kyara and jinkō agarwood, sandalwood, aromatics
t.auth: Wood grade and origin of the agarwood; school-specific utensils such as the Shino incense packet

t.d: Stickless herbal incense from monastery and Tibetan-medicine formulas.
t.tech: Extruded into lengths or coils, no bamboo core
t.mat: Himalayan herbs, often 30 or more ingredients
t.auth: Traceable lineage to a monastery or medical college; authentic Himalayan herbs

t.p: Middle Ages (tanning, scented gloves) to present
t.d: The Provençal town that grew from glove tanning into the centre of French perfume raw materials and manufacture.
t.tech: cold enfleurage of dawn-picked flowers; essential oils, concretes, absolutes, resinoids and molecular distillation
t.mat: jasmine (from the 16th century), rose, lavender, myrtle, orange blossom, mimosa
t.auth: Grasse-grown flower materials are scarce (under 30 tonnes of flowers a year by 2000), so origin claims need documentation.

t.d: Chinese cultivation of fragrant small cymbidiums as one of the Four Gentlemen, prized for scent and variegated foliage.
t.tech: pot culture of selected Jensoa cymbidiums

t.r: China (Lingnan, Shanghai, Yangzhou, Suzhou, Sichuan schools)
t.d: Chinese art of miniature trees and landscapes in containers, precursor of bonsai, saikei and hòn non bộ.
t.tech: tree penjing, rock landscape penjing, water-and-land penjing; Lingnan clip-and-grow
ctr: Wu Yee-sun, Man Lung Garden, Hong Kong

t.r: Duin- en Bollenstreek, western Netherlands (Lisse, Hillegom)
t.d: Commercial flower-bulb cultivation on the cleared coastal dunes between Haarlem and Leiden, shaped by the 17th-century tulip mania.
t.tech: field cultivation and lifting of bulbs on sandy dune soil; trade through flower auctions
t.mat: tulip, hyacinth, daffodil and other bulbs

t.d: Japanese culture of named Vanda falcata cultivars, prized by daimyō and wealthy collectors.
t.tech: selection and naming of mutant forms
t.auth: named cultivars recognised by variegation, flower and growth traits

t.d: Japanese cultivation of Iris ensata in three regional strains.
t.tech: selection of cultivars for pond and pot display
t.auth: Named cultivar of Iris ensata, assigned to a regional strain.

t.d: Vietnamese miniature landscapes of rock, plants and water resembling islands and mountains, viewed from all sides.
t.tech: rock-built mountain landscapes in water; tiểu cảnh tree scenes; cây kiểng miniature plants
t.mat: rock, plants, water, stone or concrete basins, figurines

t.d: Japanese art of growing trained miniature trees in containers, codified in named styles and size classes.
t.tech: pruning, wiring, decandling, deadwood carving, repotting into shallow pots
t.mat: juniper, pine, maple, elm, azalea; akadama and Kanuma soils
t.auth: exhibition record (Kokufu-ten), age and provenance of the tree

t.d: Japanese moss-ball planting combining the nearai (no-pot) style with bonsai and kusamono.
t.tech: ball of wet akadama and keto wrapped in moss and bound with wire or nylon

t.d: Lake Akan's large marimo balls are a protected natural monument celebrated by an Ainu festival each October; shop marimo are of European origin.
t.tech: growing loose algal balls in cool water
t.auth: collecting at Lake Akan is prohibited, so balls sold in Japan come from Europe

t.d: Chinese cultivation of the moutan tree peony, national flower from 1903 to 1929.
t.tech: selection and grafting of tree peony cultivars
t.auth: Named Chinese cultivar; Heze lists over 1,300 varieties.

t.d: Japanese planted landscape of young trees, rocks, soil and ground cover in one shallow tray, founded by Toshio Kawamoto.
t.tech: group planting with rock structure in a low tray
t.mat: young trees, rocks, ground cover, ceramic tray

t.d: Japanese culture of flowering cherries and blossom viewing, with hundreds of Sato-zakura cultivars.
t.tech: selection and grafting of cherry cultivars; blossom-viewing parties
t.auth: Cultivar names follow the Japanese Sato-zakura group; check grafted named cultivar rather than seedling.

t.p: popular by the early 7th century; ongoing
t.d: Desert falconry with saker falcons, using the blocked burqa hood with pleated back, the mangalah cuff and flat-topped block perches.
t.tech: hand-stitched blocked leather hoods

t.r: 24 states incl. UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Syria, Morocco, Kazakhstan, Mongolia, Pakistan, Korea and much of Europe
t.d: Multinational UNESCO element covering the training and flying of birds of prey, its equipment and the bond between falconer and bird.
t.tech: breeding, manning, training and flying raptors

t.p: 4th century (Nihon Shoki); flourished in the Edo period
t.d: Japanese hawking of the court and samurai class, chiefly with goshawks, organised in schools (ryū) and kept today by enthusiast clubs.
